claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you have.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 13 - and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm glad to help you assess whether you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Before I can determine eligibility, I need to understand your living situation a bit better.

**Does Alex live with you? In other words, is Alex in your care and residing at your home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's a bit complicated. Alex does live with me, but I should mention that I'm not actually in the UK at the moment - I'm living abroad right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information. Let me ask a follow-up question to better understand your situation:

**Which country are you currently living in, and do you still have a UK address or any connection to the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living abroad - we moved overseas for work. We don't have a UK address anymore, no.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Before I make my final assessment, I need to check the specific eligibility rules to ensure I give you accurate guidance. Let me review the official criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see that the rules mention living abroad may affect eligibility. I have one important question to clarify your situation:

**Are you a UK Crown servant (someone employed by the UK government on an overseas posting), or are you working for a private employer or other organization?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant - I'm working for a private company abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility. Let me explain what I've found:

According to the official Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and **you live in the UK**. 

Since you've indicated that:
- You're living abroad (not in the UK)
- You don't have a UK address
- You're not a Crown servant
- You're working for a private company

Unfortunately, the rules state that you may only be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant. As you don't fall into either of these exceptions, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

However, this could change if your circumstances alter - for example, if you were to move back to the UK or if your employment situation changed.

If you'd like to discuss your specific situation further or explore other options, I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly, as there may be specific circumstances they could advise on.

If your situation changes in the future—such as moving back to the UK—your eligibility would be reconsidered. In the meantime, if you have any questions or believe there may be special circumstances, please reach out to the Child Benefit Office directly.
